newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police quell prison disturbances; 7 dead.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police quell prison disturbances; 7 dead.

text.p: Baton-wielding police on Wednesday quelled a riot at an Istanbul prison in which five people were killed, while two inmates died in a separate disturbance in a jail in western Turkey.

"Our ambulances have carried five dead and five wounded from the Metris prison. We don't know if there are any more inside," an Istanbul health board official told Reuters. He had earlier said eight people died in Metris.
Anatolian news agency quoted Justice Minister Oltan Sungurlu as saying five prisoners died in the riot over conditions and alleged maltreatment at Metris.
Two inmates were killed in a separate incident in Alasehir jail in western Turkey, Anatolian said. The men were fatally stabbed by three prisoners who used home-made knives to take guards hostage.
Prisoners in Turkey are generally held in large, overcrowded dormitories that can hold 60 to 100 people.
Metris, an ex-military prison, holds 1,200 people despite being built for only 700.

A cordon of police stood guard around Metris jail in a rundown section of the city after the disturbance ended. Two buses full of police reinforcements and an armoured car along with about 200 prisoners' relatives waited nearby.
Gendarmerie police stormed the Istanbul jail early in the morning and seized control from inmates who had taken a warden hostage and lit fires in cells on Tuesday night.
Anxious relatives gathered outside. "We haven't been told anything," said Murat Anci, whose prisoner son was inside. Another relative fainted from the heat and stress.
Turkish television showed gendarmes beating inmates with batons and rifle butts and forcing them into a prison van after the riot.
Anatolian said the cause was the stabbing to death of an inmate on Monday night. The rioters were jailed for criminal offences and had no political demands, the agency said.
"I listened to their requests. They said they wanted better treatment and conditions," Anatolian quoted Istanbul governor Ridvan Yenisen as saying after visiting the prison.
